root_idea.summary: The central semantic orientation is the forcible or wrongful taking of something from another.
root_idea.development: The supplied lexical evidence extends this orientation to the seized thing, the taker, and the person dispossessed, as well as to related constructions of compulsion, sexual violation, and stripping hair or fur from a hide.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested noun is normalized to the classical verbal-noun citation form غَصْبٌ.

senses.definition: Forcible or wrongful taking; seizure by force.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran occurrence is the accusative verbal noun غَصْبًا, used adverbially with an act of taking to mean “by force.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take another’s property or possession wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or by force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may place the taken thing as object, or use مِنْهُ or عَلَيْهِ for the person from whom it is taken.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In legal usage, the taking of valuable, legally protected property without the owner’s permission and without stealth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The technical definition distinguishes it from theft and entrusted property and excludes things not treated as legally protected property or as having a lawful price, as well as property not legally forbidden to seize under the stated legal distinctions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To violate sexually or have sexual intercourse with someone against their will.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is attested in the construction غَصَبَهَا نَفْسَهَا / نَفْسِهَا as a forcible violation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To compel someone by force to do something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction غَصَبَ فُلَانًا عَلَى الشَّيْءِ takes the compelled person with عَلَى followed by the thing or action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove the hair or fur from a hide by plucking or peeling it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized hide-preparation usage, described as removing the hair or fur without the customary soaking or loosening processes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take something from someone by violence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This Form III usage is reported in the supplied entry without a named supporting authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be sexually violated or raped by force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The supplied evidence attests the passive constructions اُغْتُصِبَتْ نَفْسَهَا and اُغْتُصِبَتْ عَلَى نَفْسِهَا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing taken wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or by force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the result or object meaning of the noun, distinct from its verbal-noun meaning “forcible taking.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who takes something wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or by force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural form غُصَّابٌ is also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person from whom something has been taken wrongfully or by force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized passive-participial construction referring to the dispossessed person.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The unit contains the general forcible-taking sense, the associated verbal-noun sense, and a distinct legal technical definition.
Verb construction for taking property from someone by force.

cautions: No root-specific Maqayis or Mufradat entry was supplied; the root orientation is therefore based on the supplied Lane evidence.

The sole Quran occurrence is غَصْبًا, an accusative verbal noun used adverbially; the broader classical agent, result, legal, sexual, and hide-related usages are not claimed as Quranic senses of that occurrence.
